conditions.selection: Match caller status; clarify before choosing this pathway.

requirements: Classroom education may begin at 14; a learner license requires age 15 or older.
Complete the first six classroom hours and obtain the learner-stage education certificate before applying to DPS.

Bring the applicable DE-964/DEE-964/DE-964E education evidence and required identity, residency, lawful-status and SSN documentation. Parent/guardian presence or an accepted waiver/notarized application is required as specified by DPS.
Drive only with a licensed adult aged at least 21 in the front passenger seat.
Hold the learner license at least six months unless turning 18 first. Suspension extends the holding period by the suspension duration.
Complete seven hours driving instruction, seven observation hours, and 30 additional supervised practice hours including ten at night. A school package is not automatically all 44 hours.
The practice supervisor must be 21+, licensed for at least a year; the parent/guardian certifies the 30-hour practice log. Follow the approved course instructions for other logs.
Complete classroom and in-car education, the applicable learner holding period and ITTD within 90 days, then pass the skills test; DPS decides provisional issuance.
No more than one non-family passenger under 21. No driving midnight–5 a.m. except work, school activities or emergencies.
Cellphone use, including hands-free, is prohibited while driving except an emergency under the cited teen guidance.

pathways.readiness_scope: General pathway explanation only; READY does not authorize booking, establish individual eligibility or certify a particular provider.

requirements: Complete six-hour adult driver education; full teen-course alternatives are described by TDLR.
Apply at DPS, provide required documents and biometrics, pay the application fee, and pass vision, knowledge and driving skills requirements unless an applicable waiver is established.

Provide identity, Texas residency, citizenship/lawful-presence evidence and SSN as applicable, plus the application. Owned-vehicle insurance or a no-vehicle statement is specified; vehicle registration evidence at application is limited to new residents exchanging out-of-state licenses on the general DPS page.
Complete the appropriate ITD program after required education/in-car instruction and before skills testing. It does not replace driver education.
Minor teen/PTDE applicants use ITTD (two hours). Adult six-hour-course/ADE-1317 applicants use ITAD (one hour); DPS overview also identifies ITAD for ages 25+.
Present a printed ITD certificate dated within 90 days of the skills test. If the test is not passed within that window, restart the program. ITAD and ITTD are free.
Testing may be completed through an eligible third-party provider. DPS completes license issuance; a test pass alone is not a license.

Obtain TDLR instructor designation for the particular student before teaching; read the supplied program guide and select an approved parent-taught course.
Current public guidance states $20 nonrefundable per instructor/student designation application, online only. This is separate from course costs.

Bring a legally operable vehicle that passes the examiner's safety check: working signals, horn, speedometer, mirrors, doors, seatbelts and brake lights, plus weather-appropriate lights/wipers. Bring current registration and insurance; the applicant must not be an excluded driver.
Present valid identification. Unsafe vehicles may prevent testing; pets/unauthorized passengers are excluded, and dangerous or illegal maneuvers cause an automatic failure.

requirements: DPS permits driving with a valid unexpired US-state/territory, Canadian or qualifying-country license for up to 90 days after moving to Texas.

Provide identity, Texas residency, citizenship/lawful-presence evidence and SSN as applicable, plus the application. Owned-vehicle insurance or a no-vehicle statement is specified; vehicle registration evidence at application is limited to new residents exchanging out-of-state licenses on the general DPS page.

Normally present two printed documents with the applicant's name and Texas residential address; one must show at least 30 days' residency. Exchange of a valid unexpired out-of-state license/ID waives the 30-day duration, not the two-document requirement.
Surrender the recognized license and apply with Texas documents. DPS describes knowledge/skills and adult education/ITD waivers; do not sell a first-time education or test package as mandatory.
